title: SUPERHEAT: Transarterial embolization as an adjunct to structured rehabilitation for persistent pain after proximal humerus fracture (pilot RCT)
summary: Persistent shoulder pain following a fracture of the upper arm bone is common in older patients and significantly impairs quality of life, even after complete bone healing. Standard treatments such as physiotherapy, painkillers, or cortisone injections do not always provide adequate relief. New evidence suggests that abnormal blood vessels and inflammation in the shoulder joint contribute to ongoing pain. The SUPERHEAT trial investigates whether a minimally invasive procedure – in which these abnormal blood vessels are selectively blocked via a thin catheter – combined with physiotherapy can reduce pain more effectively than physiotherapy alone. A total of 80 patients from Denmark and Germany will be randomly assigned to one of two treatment groups and followed for 12 months.
conditions: Persistent shoulder pain and functional impairment following conservatively treated proximal humerus fracture

interventions.name: (Intervention): Transarterial embolization (TAE) combined with a 12-week structured physical rehabilitation (SPR) program. (Control): Structured physical rehabilitation (SPR) alone for 12 weeks, without interventional procedure.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Conservatively treated proximal humerus fracture, 6–12 months prior to screening
Persistent shoulder pain during movement (activity-based NRS ≥4) and/or functional impairment (anteversion or abduction <90°)
Age ≥60 years
DCE-MRI showing at least one of the following: pathological hypervascularity, synovitis, capsulitis
Written informed consent to participate in the study and to undergo DCE-MRI
Exclusion criteria:
Surgically treated proximal humerus fracture
One- or four-part fracture according to Neer classification
Non-union or delayed union visible on X-ray at time of screening
Rotator cuff tear or concomitant injuries on DCE-MRI requiring surgical treatment
Pre-existing major shoulder pathology unrelated to the PHF
Active infection or malignancy in the shoulder region
Contraindications to MRI or angiography contrast agent
Uncorrectable coagulopathy or renal impairment precluding contrast administration
Severe comorbidities precluding safe study participation
Participation in another interventional trial for the affected shoulder
